items.title: Phil Woods — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: my wife Jill takes care of the books so I couldn’t steal if I wanted to

ctx.x: No. The, I think the main ingredient of keeping a band together is to be fair, uh you know. Many leaders you pay the band a certain amount of money then you get a plum that pays, you know, a real plum that pays a lot of bread and you keep all the bread and you pay the band the same amount of money you were getting when you didn’t have money, you know what I mean? We’ve always shared the pie, as long as I got leader’s fee we’ve always split it into sixths; I get two sixths, and my wife Jill takes care of the books…
Also uh I think one of the successes of your group was the arrangements. You played, you move the material but you sounded like a band,
